trust_decision.summary: TOML key resolution may only walk containers the compiler itself created: lib/compiler.js must never follow a user key (__proto__/constructor) or an existing value into a prototype-bearing object (Object.prototype, Number.prototype, Date.prototype, plain arrays), and only its own null-prototype tables are legal traversal targets. At the pinned commit the only defence is that containers are made with Object.create(null); traversal never checks ownership, so a key path that reaches a scalar's __proto__ chain writes onto a real prototype.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names __proto__ key-path desynchronization and the fix commit is titled 'prevent prototype traversal during table resolution'; deepRef is the routine that walks user key paths for [table] and [[array-of-tables]] headers, returns the traversal target, and its only guard is the valueAssignments check at lib/compiler.js:196, with no check that ctx is a compiler-owned container.

fix_sites.entry_point: toml.parse() -> assign(): dotted assignment keys inside a table
toml.parse() -> setNestedKey(): dotted keys inside inline tables
helpers used by all of the above (createTable/createTableArray/isOwnedContainer/pathKey/makeFullPath/isSameOrSubPath)

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Keys literally named __proto__ or constructor are legal TOML and must stay own properties of the returned null-prototype table; an over-broad fix that rejects those key names, or returns plain {} objects, breaks the existing constructor-key test and the __proto__ own-property contract the fix itself asserts.

O6_input_shapes: table header path descending through a scalar ('[a.b.y.__proto__.__proto__]')
array-of-tables state change with a string-prefix-colliding key ('aa = 1' then '[[a]]' then '[aa.__proto__.__proto__]')
table-array path state change followed by a deeper table header (currentPath becomes an array again)
dotted assignment keys resolved by assign()'s own intermediate walk (lib/compiler.js:58-74)
quoted keys containing dots ('"a.b"') versus dotted keys (a.b), handled by quoteDottedString/pathKey
single-segment versus multi-segment keys; assign accepts a string or an array via !Array.isArray(keys) (lib/compiler.js:54)
legitimate single key '__proto__' (must become an own property, not a prototype walk)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third intermediate-key walker for a new dotted-key/table-array sub-path feature
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: assign() already implements its own target[k] descent separate from deepRef(), so a new feature branch would copy this loop and inherit its weaker scalar/null/array-only guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a defaults/merge setter that overlays parsed defaults on a caller object by reusing setNestedKey
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: setNestedKey is a second, independent key setter with its own definedKeys guard set and no ownership check; a merge/defaults route would naturally reuse it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a parseFile/parseWithOptions wrapper that feeds a caller-owned target object or a pre-built AST into compile
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: parse() is a five-line wrapper and compile() already accepts caller-built nodes (lib/compiler.js:2,222-224), so adding options there is the obvious extension point.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321): object-prototype property injection during TOML key-path resolution

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject any key named __proto__ (or switch result objects from Object.create(null) to plain {}), which either breaks legitimate __proto__/constructor keys or leaves prototype walks through a scalar's __proto__ chain open.

out_of_scope_notes: test/spec-test.js:59-76 builds a plain-object typeMap keyed by user-derived TOML path strings; it is a test harness (test/ is excluded from the published package by package.json:7-11) and not the advisory's sink.
